summary: A description of a proposed modular graphics and text display with a plasma panel and a small processor. It could work as an intelligent terminal, as a passive terminal imitating other displays, or as an offline minicomputer.

eli5.summary: A screen with a built-in little computer that can show pictures and words, act like older screens, or work by itself.

subtitle: A display terminal combining a plasma screen and embedded processor

tldr.problem: Early display terminals lacked local processing and memory, requiring constant refresh from a host and limiting interactive use.
tldr.mechanism: The DS-1 combines a 512-by-512 line plasma display panel with built-in memory and a minicomputer processor, allowing it to function as an intelligent terminal, a passive terminal emulating other displays, or a standalone offline system.
tldr.outcome: A flexible, high-resolution display terminal with local processing power suitable for text editing, graphics, and data visualization over the ARPANET.

facts.label: Display resolution
facts.value: 512 by 512 lines at 60 lines per inch

facts.label: Modem speed
facts.value: 0 to 1800 bps (full duplex) or 0 to 1200 bps (half duplex)

today: RFC 296 describes an early intelligent terminal combining local processing with network connectivity. The DS-1's architecture of plasma display, embedded processor, and network modem presaged the workstations and graphical terminals that became common in later decades.

sections.title: The DS-1 System
sections.content: The DS-1 Display System is a modular graphics and alphanumeric terminal proposed by Owens-Illinois. It combines three components: a plasma display/memory panel with 512 by 512 lines at 60 lines per inch resolution, a Raytheon minicomputer processor with 1.6-microsecond cycle time, and a keyboard. The system can operate in three modes: as an intelligent terminal processing data from a network or host, as a passive terminal translating existing display commands and data structures for its plasma panel, or as an offline minicomputer for local work.
sections.eli5: A new kind of screen and computer system that can show sharp pictures, work with data from other computers, or work all by itself.

sections.title: Display and Processor Components
sections.content:
The plasma display panel is constructed from two pieces of glass with fine gold electrodes, sealed with a neon-filled gap. Each point on the display can be individually turned on or off and retains its state through the panel's inherent memory, eliminating the need for constant refresh. The Owens-Illinois drive electronics sustain cells at approximately 130 volts and use multiplexed address circuits. Writing and erasing each point takes about 20 microseconds, allowing vector drawing at more than 800 inches per second and character display at about 1400 characters per second.

The Raytheon processor includes 2048 words of RAM for programs, 64 words of ROM for bootstrap code, and a 12-bit program counter and memory address register. The processor communicates with the display, keyboard, and modems through a TTL-compatible I/O bus with 16 parallel data lines, device selection, function codes, and status monitoring.
sections.eli5: The screen uses electricity to write dots that stay on without flickering, and the processor tells it what to draw and listens for typing.

sections.title: Software and Communication
sections.content:
The DS-1 runs software for text editing, vector generation, character display, and data management. The processor handles communication protocols, string manipulation, character translation, and vector construction to ensure the character stream to the modem remains compatible with host computers while the keyboard and display operate efficiently locally.

The system includes a modem operating at 0 to 1800 bps in four-wire full-duplex mode or 0 to 1200 bps in half-duplex mode, and an optional cassette tape recorder for program loading. The processor supports 19 instruction types including data movement, logical operations, condition checking, input/output, jump control, and indexing, with single-level interrupt capability.
sections.eli5: Programs running inside the DS-1 translate between what you type, what the screen shows, and what messages go to other computers.

sections.title: Key Advantages
sections.content:
The plasma panel's inherent memory and selective erase capability eliminate the need for refresh or buffer memory, distinguishing it from storage tube displays. High contrast, crisp line dimensions, no jitter or flicker, and support for rear projection of optical data make it suitable for normal laboratory environments. The 8.5 by 8.5 inch active area at 60 lines per inch provides resolution sufficient for highly readable characters and graphics without distortion.

The flexible mechanical design allows independent orientation of the keyboard and display module relative to the processor. The system's expandable memory and local processing enable sophisticated local operations while maintaining network compatibility.
sections.eli5: The plasma screen does not flicker, stays sharp, and can show both computer images and pictures from slides. The built-in computer means you can do work locally without waiting for the network.

references.text: Liddle, D., "DS-1 Display System", RFC 296, January 1972.
